statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 13% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, with Stress 52% elevated and Confidence 88% high.
recommendation: Conditions are described as low tail risk on a contained Globex tape holding inside an 86-point overnight band, set against an unresolved US-Iran energy shock that has lifted WTI roughly 10% on the week and a September policy debate framed as hike-versus-hold. The single mapped danger window is the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September through 14:30Z, covering the release and the first hour of U.S. cash trade.
headline: NQ 29,560.75 holds the upper half of an 86-point Globex band ahead of the 12:30Z August employment report
body: The Globex session remains contained and mildly firm. NQ traded 29,560.75 at 03:15Z, up 36.00 points or 0.12%, inside an 86-point 29,482.00-29,568.00 band on roughly 19.8k contracts. The contract sits near the top of that band, but a 0.29% overnight range on minimal volume is a slow drift rather than the persistent no-retracement structure Tail measures, so Tail holds at 13% and the dominant mode stays normal. E-mini S&P 500 futures corroborate at 7,758.00, up 0.04%. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Thursday at 29,482.32, up 1.16%, after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signalled he would be inclined to hold rates steady; the index settled 56 points below its 29,538.76 session high, which is the opposite of an extreme-holding close. Cross-assets are broadly supportive of equities: VIX fell 5.79% to 14.32, the 10-year yield eased 3.4 basis points to 4.762% and the 2-year stood at 4.39% on the latest H.15 column. The clear conflict is energy. WTI is $91.89, up about 10% on the week, and Brent traded near $97.29 after renewed US-Iran strikes cut Strait of Hormuz transits to six commodity vessels on Wednesday against a ten-day average near thirteen. That conflict is scored as elevated Stress rather than elevated Tail, because a headline-driven energy premium is not observed directional efficiency in the index. The August employment report at 12:30Z is the session's defining checkpoint, with consensus near 53,000 to 58,000 payrolls, an unemployment rate of 4.1% and a forecast range running from about -25,000 to +125,000. Event magnitude and dispersion of that size raise Stress and lower Confidence in the event hours rather than pre-emptively raising Tail. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 00:28Z and is beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale and excluded; this assessment rests on independently fetched primary quotes, yields, oil, the U.S. calendar and verified reporting.

lookbackSummary: Every one of the past 24 clock-hours carries a published Claude assessment, and the state was green in 20 of them. Tail held between 12% and 15% from the Asian session through the European morning and into the early U.S. afternoon while Stress drifted from the high 50s down to the low 50s. The state moved to yellow at 15:00Z and 16:00Z with Tail at 21% and 20% as the index held near its session extreme after the Waller remarks, returned to green at 17:00Z during consolidation, went yellow once more at 18:00Z on a fresh session high with Tail 21%, then unwound steadily through the U.S. close. Tail printed 12% at 23:00Z, 00:00Z and 01:00Z, its lowest of the window, and 13% at 02:00Z. The dominant mode ran normal through the overnight and European hours, mixed around the early U.S. afternoon, trend-up from 15:00Z to 21:00Z, and back to normal once the cash session settled 56 points below its high.
outlookSummary: The near path keeps Tail in the low band while Globex trades inside an 86-point band on thin volume and the cash session has already settled below its high, holding 13% through the remaining Asian hours as participation stays minimal. Risk rebuilds gradually across the European morning into the August employment report at 12:30Z, which anchors the mapped danger window through 14:30Z and covers both the release and the first hour of U.S. cash trade. Tail is deliberately capped at the top of the watch band across 12:00Z through 15:00Z because forecast dispersion and event magnitude raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than establishing an observed one-way path; the July 2026 precedent of a large payroll surprise that still permitted mean reversion supports that cap. From 16:00Z the forecast assumes orderly absorption into a defined post-event range and steps Tail back below the block threshold, with the 19:00Z power hour treated as a checkpoint rather than an amplifier. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final six hours describe a dormant state with no continuous price path, where residual Stress is weekend-gap exposure into the Sunday 22:00Z reopen rather than live structural risk.
